statement: Which one of these numbers is odd: 10, 12, 14, 16 or 15?

choices.misconception: I looked at the 1 at the front instead of the last digit.
I thought a number containing a 1 must be odd.
I chose a number that can still be shared into two equal piles.
I chose the largest even number, thinking size mattered.

hints: Odd numbers cannot be shared into two equal piles.
Look only at the last digit. A number is odd when it ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, whatever the rest of the number looks like.
Try sharing each number into two equal piles. Only one of them has a leftover.

solutions.reliable: A number is odd when sharing it into two equal piles leaves one over, and that depends only on the last digit. Only 15 ends in an odd digit. The idea to keep: the last digit decides, so the front of the number can be ignored.

whyOnTest: Reading the wrong digit is the first mistake students make with odd and even, and two choices are built from it.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
